  - No assumptions on portfolio development, no quantified contribution to total emissions reductions, and Scope 3 share not specified due to sector-based targets.
- Sectoral financed-emission targets to 2030 under NZBA: six sectors—mortgages, commercial real estate, power generation, oil & gas, steel, and a new 2024 target for shipping; five are intensity-based; sectors defined per PCAF; targets not third-party validated; outcomes influenced by client emissions, exposure, and client asset sizes.

Weighted average carbon intensity declined from 2023 to 2024, and the share of investments in SBTi-verified companies increased.

- Asset management (Swedbank Robur Fonder): Net-zero approach with fossil fuel exclusions (coal, oil, gas), daily compliance controls, and active engagement with high-emitting holdings lacking SBTi-verified targets; rising share of SBTi-verified investees and declining weighted average carbon intensity from 2023 to 2024.
- Own operations: 2024 review to map scope 3 (Purchased goods and services) emissions across the supplier base to enable more effective supply-chain emission reductions.
- Metrics and targets (E1-4) for lending:
  - Target outcomes reported using 2023 customer emissions data due to 2024 data unavailability; financed emissions (E1-6) use 2024 exposure with latest customer data.
  - Targets aligned with NZBA 1.5°C trajectories; approved by the CEO and reviewed by the Board; stakeholders consulted at a high level but not for target-setting.
  - No assumptions made about portfolio development; contribution to total emissions reduction not yet quantified; scope 3 share not specified because targets apply to selected sectors.
  - Participation in EEMI, NZBA, PCAF, and Poseidon Principles.
- Six sectoral climate targets for financed emissions by 2030 under NZBA, mostly intensity-based, with a new 2024 target for shipping; sectors covered: mortgages, commercial real estate, power generation, oil & gas, steel, and shipping. Targets use PCAF definitions and are not third-party validated.
- Mortgages sector target:
  - Reduce financed emissions intensity (kgCO2e/m2) by 39% by 2030 vs. 2019; 2050 ambition of −89%.
  - Covers properties’ scope 1 and 2 emissions across Swedbank’s four home markets; aligned with CRREM 1.5°C intensity trajectory and NZBA guidance.
  - 2019 baseline recalibrated to 10.0 kgCO2e/m2; 2023 shows a 6% intensity reduction vs. baseline.
  - Swedish and Baltic portfolios both reduced intensity (−14% and −11%), but Group-level progress tempered by higher growth in the higher-intensity Baltic portfolio.
  - Key future drivers: continued energy-efficiency upgrades, better energy performance certificate (EPC) data, and phasing out fossil heating; actions include Hemma advisory support and participation in expert groups to improve property energy data.
  - In the Baltics, incentives for energy class A properties and efforts to improve EPC coverage; external factors like district heating carbon intensity and EU EPBD developments may affect progress.

nodes.title: Sector target – Mortgages
nodes.heading: Sector target – Mortgages
nodes.start_phrase: About the target: Swedbank has a target to reduce its financed emission intensity (kgCO2e/m2) from mortgages by 39 per cent by 2030, compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines Swedbank’s climate targets for financed emissions across key lending sectors, progress through 2023, and a detailed focus on the Mortgage portfolio.

- Portfolio-wide targets and methodology:
  - Sector-specific 2030 targets set mainly as intensity reductions versus a 2019 baseline (shipping baseline 2022); oil and gas uses an absolute emissions target.
  - Reporting covers selected parts of GHG Protocol Category 15; no use of carbon credits.
  - Methods align with the Net-Zero Banking Alliance; emissions are expressed in CO2e and include multiple GHGs depending on source data.
  - Results reported for 2021–2023; 2024 customer emissions data not yet available. No absolute emissions forecast for intensity-only sectors.

- 2030 sector targets and 2023 progress (vs. 2019 baseline unless noted):
  - Mortgages: intensity target −39%; 2023 down ~6%.
  - Commercial real estate: intensity target −43%; 2023 down ~12%.
  - Power generation: intensity target −59%; 2023 down ~50%.
  - Oil and gas (E&P and refining): absolute emissions −50%; 2023 down ~53%.
  - Steel: intensity target −29%; 2023 down ~30%.
  - Shipping: target to reach 0% alignment delta by 2030 vs. IMO’s most ambitious “striving” trajectory; current positive alignment delta remains; baseline year 2022.

- Mortgage sector deep dive (62% of loan portfolio by gross carrying amount):
  - Targets: −39% intensity by 2030 and −89% by 2050 vs. 2019; scope 1 and 2 of collateralized residential properties and tenant-owner associations across Swedbank’s four home markets; pathway based on CRREM 1.5°C.
  - Baseline update: 2024 recalculation improved data quality and adjusted 2019 baseline from 9.2 to 10.0 kgCO2e/m2.
  - 2023 outcome: −6% vs. 2019; Swedish portfolio −14% and Baltic portfolio −11%, but higher growth in the Baltics (with higher intensity) tempered group-level improvement.
  - Key drivers and actions: accelerate energy efficiency upgrades, expand availability and quality of energy performance certificates (EPCs), phase out fossil heating. Initiatives include customer advisory support via Hemma, participation in an expert group with Swedish authorities to improve EPC data, pricing incentives for A-class properties in the Baltics, and efforts to raise EPC coverage.
  - Dependencies and risks: evolution of CO2 intensity in energy sources (e.g., district heating) and impacts of new regulations like the EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD).

Overall, the document presents measurable sector goals, notes solid progress in power generation, oil and gas, and steel, modest gains in real estate and mortgages, and ongoing alignment work in shipping, while detailing data, methodology, and levers to accelerate decarbonization—especially within the large Mortgage portfolio.

nodes.title: Sector target – Commercial real estate
nodes.heading: Sector target – Commercial real estate
nodes.start_phrase: About the target: Swedbank aims to reduce its financed emission intensity (kgCO2e/m2) from commercial real estates by 43 per cent by 2030, compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Swedbank’s sector-specific climate targets and progress for Commercial Real Estate and Oil & Gas within its loan portfolio, using 2019 as the baseline year and aligning with 1.5°C pathways.

- Commercial Real Estate (about 15% of loan portfolio, share of Gross Carrying Amount):
  - Target: Reduce financed emission intensity (kgCO2e/m2, scopes 1 and 2) by 43% by 2030 and by 91% by 2050 versus 2019.
  - Methodology: Intensity-based CRREM 1.5°C trajectory; aligned with NZBA; emissions measured in CO2e, with gases included dependent on underlying data.
  - Data update: 2024 improvements led to baseline adjustment from 25.1 to 22.8 kgCO2e/m2; prior outcome for 2022 revised from a 17% to an 8% reduction.
  - 2023 outcome: 12% reduction vs 2019.
  - Actions and drivers: Increasing share of higher energy-class buildings, energy efficiency upgrades, advisory via Ramboll, improved data through more energy declarations, requiring EPCs and transition plans for new financing; Baltic portfolio has reduced intensity but needs faster progress, with a control process linking new loans to credible energy improvement plans.
  - Note: 2024 outcome not yet available; details on calculations on pages 111–113.

- Oil and Gas (<1% of loan portfolio):
  - Target: Reduce absolute financed emissions (scopes 1, 2, and 3) by 50% by 2030 and by 99% by 2050 versus 2019; applies to large customers (thresholds defined by turnover/assets and exposure).
  - Methodology: OECM Europe 1.5°C trajectory (67% probability), supported by NZBA; comparison to IEA NZ2050 (50% probability); emissions in CO2e, gases per customer reporting.
  - Outcome: 53% reduction since 2019—2030 target already achieved—primarily due to a strategic reduction in exposure to oil & gas extraction; remaining exposure focused on a few refineries with transition plans.
  - Ongoing: Continued monitoring of financed emissions, evaluation of customer transition plans, and periodic review of target scope and levels.

- Cross-cutting notes:
  - Baseline year 2019 chosen to avoid Covid-19 distortions.
  - Emissions coverage and data quality are critical; gases included depend on available data/reporting.
  - Lending and measurement pertain to Swedbank’s home markets.
  - Visual trajectories indicate planned reductions to 2030; 2024 outcomes not yet reported.

nodes.title: Sector target – Oil and Gas
nodes.heading: Sector target – Oil and Gas
nodes.start_phrase: About the target: Swedbank has a target to reduce absolute financed emissions (million tCO2e) from oil and gas (including exploration, production and refining) by 50 per cent by 2030 compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Document scope: Excerpt from Swedbank’s Annual and Sustainability Report 2024 describing sector-level climate targets, methodologies, data treatments, and progress for the Commercial Real Estate (CRE) and Oil & Gas portfolios.

- Portfolio shares and metrics:
  - Commercial Real Estate: 15% of loan portfolio; target metric is financed emissions intensity (kgCO2e/m2), covering borrowers’ scope 1 and 2.
  - Oil & Gas: <1% of loan portfolio; target metric is absolute financed emissions (million tCO2e), covering borrowers’ scope 1, 2, and 3 for large customers.

- Targets and timelines:
  - CRE: Reduce financed emission intensity by 43% by 2030 vs 2019; 91% reduction by 2050.
  - Oil & Gas: Reduce absolute financed emissions by 50% by 2030 vs 2019; 99% reduction by 2050.
  - 2019 baseline chosen to avoid Covid-19 distortions.

- Methodologies and scope:
  - CRE: Intensity-based pathway aligned with CRREM 1.5°C trajectory; consistent with NZBA guidance. Applies to revenue-generating properties (retail, office, sports facilities, industrial, multi-family) in Swedbank’s home markets. Uses CO2e; included gases depend on underlying data sources.
  - Oil & Gas: Target calibrated to OECM Europe 1.5°C pathway (67% probability), contrasted with IEA NZ2050 (50%). Applies to large customers across home markets; included gases depend on customers’ reporting.

- Data quality and baseline adjustments:
  - In 2024, CRE data and calculation improvements revised the 2019 baseline from 25.1 to 22.8 kgCO2e/m2, which changed the 2022 outcome from a 17% to an 8% reduction. 2024 outcomes are not yet available for both sectors.

- Outcomes and progress:
  - CRE: By 2023, a 12% reduction vs 2019. Swedish portfolio intensity decreased; Baltic portfolio also decreased but must accelerate to meet 2030 target.
  - Oil & Gas: Financed emissions down 53% since 2019, already exceeding the 2030 target, mainly due to a strategic reduction in exposure to oil & gas extraction. Remaining exposure is to a few refineries with transition plans; ongoing monitoring and target scope reviews continue.

- Implementation actions and enablers:
  - CRE: Focus on financing higher energy class properties and driving efficiency in existing stock; advisory support via Ramboll; increasing energy declaration/EPC coverage to improve data; considering requirements for EPCs and transition plans in new financing. In the Baltics, a control process assesses building energy performance and emissions at origination; new loans to low-performing buildings require credible upgrade plans.
  - Emphasis across sectors on data availability and quality for tracking and achieving targets.

- References:
  - Measurement and calculation details indicated as available on pages 111–113 of the report.

nodes.title: Sector target – Power Generation
nodes.heading: Sector target – Power Generation
nodes.start_phrase: About the target: Swedbank has a target to reduce its financed emission inten -sity (tCO2e/MWh) from power generation by 59 per cent by 2030 compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Document segment outlines Swedbank’s sectoral decarbonization targets for Power Generation and Steel, each representing less than 1% of the loan portfolio (share of Gross Carrying Amount).
- Baseline year for both sectors is 2019, chosen to avoid Covid-19 distortions; 2024 outcomes are not yet available.
- Methodology: financed emissions calculated in CO2e and include multiple greenhouse gases, depending on client reporting; targets align with NZBA guidance and science-based reduction pathways.
- Power Generation target: reduce financed emission intensity (tCO2e/MWh) by 59% by 2030 and 99% by 2050 versus 2019. Target is set using the One Earth Climate Model (OECM) European trajectory (67% probability of limiting warming to 1.5°C), contrasted with IEA NZ2050 (50% probability). Coverage includes large customers across home markets and customers’ scope 1 and 2 emissions.
- Steel target: reduce financed emission intensity (tCO2e/tonne steel) by 29% by 2030 and 94% by 2050 versus 2019. Target based on a combination of OECM and IEA NZ2050 global trajectories, reflecting the portfolio’s global exposure. Coverage includes large customers and customers’ scope 1 and 2 emissions.
- Large customer definition: (1) annual turnover > SEK 500m or total assets > SEK 1,000m; and (2) exposure commitments > SEK 8m.
- 2024 portfolio-wide financed emissions recalculation introduced stricter use of consolidated vs company-level data, leading to baseline adjustments:
  - Power Generation baseline updated from 0.17 to 0.16 tCO2e/MWh.
  - Steel baseline updated from 0.89 to 0.97 tCO2e/tonne.
- Outcomes to date (vs 2019 baseline):
  - Power Generation: 50% reduction in emission intensity by 2023, driven by client divestment of fossil assets, balance sheet changes affecting attribution, and growth in renewables (notably in the Baltics).
  - Steel: 30% reduction in emission intensity by 2023, due to increased exposure to lower-intensity companies and clients’ emission reductions; portfolio concentration means single-client exposure shifts can materially affect intensity.
- Forward focus: expand financing for renewable power generation and ensure all portfolio customers have credible transition plans; continue monitoring steel portfolio intensity and manage exposure impacts.
- Further methodological details and measurement approaches are referenced on pages 111–113 of the report.

nodes.title: Sector target – Steel
nodes.heading: Sector target – Steel
nodes.start_phrase: About the target: Swedbank has a target to reduce its financed emission inten -sity (tCO2e/t steel) from steel production by 29 per cent by 2030 compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Sector-specific decarbonization targets for Swedbank’s financed emissions in Power Generation and Steel, each representing less than 1% of the loan portfolio (share of Gross Carrying Amount).
- Targets and timelines:
  - Power Generation: Reduce financed emission intensity (tCO2e/MWh) by 59% by 2030 vs. 2019; 99% by 2050.
  - Steel: Reduce financed emission intensity (tCO2e/tonne) by 29% by 2030 vs. 2019; 94% by 2050.
  - 2019 chosen as the baseline to avoid Covid-19 distortions; 2024 outcome not available.
- Scope and coverage:
  - Targets based on CO2e and include multiple greenhouse gases, dependent on customer reporting.
  - Emissions covered: customers’ Scope 1 and 2.
  - Applies to lending to large customers in all Swedbank home markets, defined as turnover > SEK 500m or total assets > SEK 1,000m, and exposure commitments > SEK 8m.
- Methodology and alignment:
  - Power Generation target aligned to the One Earth Climate Model (OECM) European trajectory (67% probability of limiting warming to 1.5°C) and contrasted with IEA NZ2050 (50% probability).
  - Steel target set using a combination of OECM and IEA NZ2050 global trajectories.
  - Methodology aligned with the Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA) guidelines.
- 2024 methodological update:
  - Comprehensive recalculation of financed emissions for the entire lending portfolio with stricter rules favoring consolidated over company-level data.
  - Baseline adjustments:
    - Power Generation: 0.17 → 0.16 tCO2e/MWh (2019).
    - Steel: 0.89 → 0.97 tCO2e/tonne (2019).
  - Further calculation details referenced on pages 111–113.
- Outcomes to date:
  - Power Generation (to 2023): 50% reduction in financed emission intensity vs. 2019, driven by rapid customer divestment of fossil assets, balance sheet changes affecting attribution to Swedbank, and growth in renewables (notably in the Baltics). Forward focus on expanding renewable financing and ensuring credible customer transition plans.
  - Steel (to latest update): 30% reduction vs. 2019, reflecting increased exposure to lower-intensity companies and customer emission cuts. On track with target. Portfolio concentration means changes in single-customer exposure can materially affect intensity. Ongoing monitoring and emphasis on credible transition plans.

nodes.title: Sector target – Shipping
nodes.heading: Sector target – Shipping
nodes.start_phrase: About the target: During the year, Swedbank adopted a Group-wide climate target for the shipping portfolio in order to integrate climate considerations in the Group’s loan decisions on financing for shipping.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Swedbank’s climate target for its Shipping sector loan portfolio, which is less than 1% of total loans.
- Target: Achieve 0% alignment delta by 2030 versus the International Maritime Organization’s “striving for” reduction trajectory, meaning the portfolio is fully aligned with the pathway. Baseline year: 2022.
- Framework and metric: Target set under the Poseidon Principles; alignment measured using the Annual Efficiency Ratio (AER) in g CO2e/tonne-nautical mile.
- Scope and coverage: Applies to vessels ≥5,000 gross tonnage; covers “well-to-wake” emissions (scope 1 and upstream scope 3 from fuel consumption) for CO2, CH4, and N2O across all Swedbank home markets.
- Context: The IMO pathway includes a sector goal of net-zero by 2050 but is not yet fully aligned with a 1.5°C scenario; Swedbank will revise its target as Poseidon Principles methodologies and emission trajectories improve.
- Baseline and progress: 2022 alignment delta was 39.5%. It decreased to 17.7% during the year (driven by portfolio changes and methodology improvements for passenger and roll-on/roll-off segments). Outcome for 2024 is not available.
- Actions to reach 2030: Prioritize financing customers with credible transition plans and support fleet renewal via modern and new vessels with fossil-free potential.
- Sector emissions overview (non-shipping): A table summarizes lending and financed emissions for sectors with climate targets—mortgages, commercial real estate, power generation, oil & gas, and steel—showing 2023 portfolio coverage by targets and scopes, plus financed emissions for 2023, 2022, 2021, and baseline 2019. Shipping is excluded due to lack of historical financed emissions.
- Key figures from the table (2023): 
  - Mortgages: 99% coverage; scopes 1 & 2; 0.51 MtCO2e.
  - Commercial real estate: 86% coverage; scopes 1 & 2; 0.37 MtCO2e.
  - Power generation: 87% coverage; scope 1; 0.50 MtCO2e.
  - Oil & gas (E&P and refining): 100% coverage; scopes 1, 2 & 3; 2.99 MtCO2e.
  - Steel: 96% coverage; scopes 1 & 2; 0.18 MtCO2e.
- Methodological notes: Emissions are calculated using gross carrying amount for mortgages and commercial real estate, and carrying amount plus off-balance exposure for power generation, oil & gas, and steel; “major customers” thresholds are defined for inclusion.

nodes.title: Scope of the targets
nodes.heading: Scope of the targets
nodes.start_phrase: The table below provides an overview of total lending by sector as well as financed emissions for sectors covered by climate targets.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Swedbank’s sector climate target for Shipping and how it fits within the bank’s broader portfolio-level climate targets and financed emissions coverage.

- Shipping sector target:
  - Portfolio share: <1% of the loan portfolio.
  - Goal: 0% alignment delta by 2030 versus the IMO “striving for” decarbonization trajectory (Poseidon Principles methodology).
  - Baseline year: 2022; initial alignment delta 39.5%.
  - Outcome: alignment delta reduced to 17.7% during the year; driven by portfolio changes and methodology improvements (notably for passenger and roll-on/roll-off vessels) under the Poseidon Principles. Note: 2024 outcome not available in the chart.
  - Scope and coverage: vessels ≥5,000 gross tonnage; well-to-wake emissions (scope 1 and upstream scope 3 from fuel consumption); gases CO2, CH4, N2O; all home markets.
  - Method: Annual Efficiency Ratio (AER) in g CO2e/tonne-nautical mile.
  - Context: IMO path targets net-zero by 2050 but is not yet fully 1.5°C-aligned; Swedbank will revise targets as improved trajectories become available via Poseidon Principles.
  - Delivery approach: prioritize financing for clients with credible transition plans; support fleet renewal and new builds with fossil-free potential.

- Scope of climate targets across the lending portfolio:
  - Sectors with targets: mortgages, commercial real estate, power generation, oil & gas, steel, shipping (chosen per NZBA guidance and portfolio significance).
  - Coverage: 79% of gross carrying amount and 81% of total exposure under targets.
  - Financed emissions coverage: 35% of customer scope 1 & 2; 28% including scope 3; using sector-relevant scopes (scope 1 & 2 for all, plus scope 3 for oil & gas and vehicle manufacturing), coverage is 51%.
  - Shipping is excluded from the financed emissions table due to lack of historical calculations.

- 2023 lending and financed emissions for sectors with targets (excl. shipping):
  - Mortgages: SEK 1,126,839m; 99% covered; scopes 1 & 2; 0.51 MtCO2e (0.51 in 2022; 0.50 in 2021; 0.48 in 2019).
  - Commercial real estate: SEK 296,151m; 86% covered; scopes 1 & 2; 0.37 MtCO2e (0.40; 0.38; 0.36).
  - Power generation: SEK 30,776m; 87% covered; scope 1; 0.50 MtCO2e (0.89; 0.64; 1.18).
  - Oil & gas (exploration, production, refining): SEK 4,543m; 100% covered; scopes 1, 2 & 3; 2.99 MtCO2e (2.89; 4.63; 6.36).
  - Steel: SEK 5,478m; 96% covered; scopes 1 & 2; 0.18 MtCO2e (0.19; 0.24; 0.27).

- Methodology and measurement notes:
  - Mortgages and commercial real estate: financed emissions based on gross carrying amount (PCAF).
  - Other sectors: financed emissions based on total exposure to better reflect commitments.
  - Climate targets for oil & gas, power generation, steel, and shipping are set on total exposure.

- Reasons for relatively low financed emissions coverage:
  - Mortgage and property books are less carbon-intensive.
  - Limited exposure to high-carbon sectors (no coal; minimal oil & gas refining).
  - Large SME share with limited emissions data necessitating PCAF estimates, which may overstate emissions, inflating the share outside targeted sectors.

- External factors influencing target outcomes:
  - Dependence on client transitions; key drivers include technology cost declines, regulation and EU ETS, market demand for sustainable products, and investor pressure.
  - System dependencies: availability of renewable energy and fossil-free fuels.
  - Sector specifics: steel and shipping rely on new technologies (fossil-free steel, fossil-free vessels); Baltic real estate depends on national energy mix shifts.
  - Phase-out of fossil fuels and rapid technology adoption are prerequisites to meet financed emissions targets.

- Visuals referenced:
  - Planned decline of alignment delta to 0% by 2030 for shipping.
  - Portfolio breakdowns of carrying amount, exposure, and financed emissions by sector (mortgages, commercial real estate, oil & gas, shipping, power generation, steel, other).

nodes.title: External factors that can affect the outcome of targets
nodes.heading: External factors that can affect the outcome of targets
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank’s ability to achieve its climate targets within the loan portfolio is hea vily dependent on its customers making the transition.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Swedbank’s 2024 financed emissions profile and climate targets within its lending portfolio, by sector and emissions scope.
- Targeted sectors (six): Mortgages, Commercial real estate, Oil & gas, Shipping, Power generation, Steel. Vehicle manufacturing is included in “Other” and not covered by sector targets.
- Measurement approach (PCAF-aligned):
  - Mortgages and Commercial real estate: financed emissions based on gross carrying amount.
  - Other sectors: financed emissions based on total exposure; climate targets for Oil & gas, Power generation, Steel, and Shipping are also based on total exposure.
- Portfolio coverage by targets:
  - 79% of gross carrying amount and 81% of total exposure are within sector targets.
  - Targets cover 35% of financed emissions (customers’ Scope 1 & 2) and 28% when Scope 3 is included.
  - Using “most relevant scopes” per sector (Scopes 1 & 2 for all, plus Scope 3 for Oil & gas and automotive), targets cover 51% of financed emissions.
- Reasons coverage of financed emissions appears low:
  - Mortgages and property are comparatively less carbon-intensive.
  - Limited exposure to high-carbon sectors (no coal; only minor oil & gas refinery exposure).
  - Large SME share with limited company-specific emissions data, leading to reliance on PCAF estimates that may overstate emissions, inflating non-target sectors’ share.
- External dependencies and drivers affecting target outcomes:
  - Relies on clients’ transition pace.
  - Enablers include tech advances lowering green costs, regulation and EU ETS, growing demand for sustainable products/services, and investor pressure.
  - Sectoral dependencies: access to renewable energy and fossil-free fuels; steel and shipping depend on new tech (fossil-free steel production, new vessel types); Baltic real estate depends on national energy mix shifts.
  - Achieving targets requires fossil fuel phase-out and rapid technology adoption.
- Visuals referenced: 2024 charts showing sector shares of gross carrying amount, total exposure, and financed emissions (Scopes 1&2; 1,2&3; and a sector-relevant scope mix), with results expressed as SEKm and MtCO2e (exposure-based).
- Governance: Swedbank continually reviews targets to align the lending portfolio with the 1.5°C pathway; further detail in section E1-4.

nodes.title: Asset management
nodes.heading: Asset management
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank Robur Fonder has adopted interim targets within its climate strategy in three areas: reduced greenhouse gas emissions, climate solutions and engagement, summarised below in points 1–3.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Swedbank Robur Fonder’s climate strategy and targets within asset management, as presented in the 2024 Annual and Sustainability Report.
- Portfolio coverage and metric: Target applies to 97% of the (Swedish) fund portfolio; aims to reduce weighted average carbon intensity (scope 1 and 2 of holdings) by 50% by 2030 from a 2019 baseline, using an intensity metric (tCO2e/USDm).
- Overall climate ambition: Align fund management with the 1.5°C pathway by 2025 and reach net‑zero emissions by 2040, following the Paris Aligned Investment Initiative’s Net Zero Investment Framework (NZIF).
- Interim targets (three areas):
  1) Emissions and net zero: Halve emissions by 2030; strive for net zero by 2040. Increase share of AUM invested in companies with net‑zero targets to 60% by 2030 and 100% by 2040.
  2) Climate solutions: Increase investments in renewable energy to 1.4% of AUM by 2030 and 3.8% by 2040.
  3) Engagement: Conduct dialogues with companies in material sectors responsible for 70% of financed emissions, expanding to more sectors over time.
- Methodology and scenarios: Targets based on IEA’s Net Zero 2050 (NZ2050) scenario; 2019 baseline aligned with NZAM recommendations; measurement and calculation details referenced elsewhere in the report.
- Governance: Climate Strategy approved by the CEO; targets set in line with industry best practice.
- Reporting and limitations: Targets are not third‑party audited; no changes to targets, metrics, methods, assumptions, limitations, sources, or baseline reported. Scope 3 cannot be quantified. Emissions data (E1‑6) underpin reduction targets.
- Stakeholder input: Ongoing stakeholder dialogue informs target development, though stakeholders do not set targets.

nodes.title: Target for asset management
nodes.heading: Target for asset management
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank Robur Fonder’s Climate Strategy, approved by the CEO of Swedbank Robur Fonder, specifies the company’s overall climate targets and interim targets.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Swedbank Robur Fonder’s asset management climate strategy and targets, coverage, methodologies, and engagement approach.
- Portfolio coverage and scope:
  - Targets cover 97% of the Swedish fund portfolio.
  - Emissions coverage includes holdings’ scope 1 and scope 2; scope 3 cannot be quantified.

nodes.title: Own operations
nodes.heading: Own operations
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank has a target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from its own opera -tions by 60 per cent by 2030 compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Swedbank sets an absolute target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from its own operations by 60% by 2030 versus the 2019 baseline. The target covers scope 1, scope 2 (market-based), and selected scope 3 categories: business travel; security transport services; upstream emissions from energy use and from company-owned vehicles; waste management; water consumption; and paper consumption. Gases included are CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, and CFCs (refrigerants). The target applies across all home markets and operations in Norway, Finland, China, and the USA. No carbon credits are used.
- Baseline, governance, and methodology: 2019 was chosen as a pre-Covid baseline. The target was set by internal experts and is not third-party validated. It is defined in absolute terms, aligns with GHG Protocol inventory boundaries, and the emissions reported in section E1-6 form the basis. Proportions by scope are not specified due to data constraints at the time of target setting.
- Data scope evolution and reporting: Since 2019, the emissions measurement scope has expanded with better data availability. From 2022, emissions from IT equipment are included in measurement but excluded from the target (4,879 tCO2e in 2024). Historical data for 2022 and 2023 were revised to align with the target scope for clearer progress tracking.
- Performance and trends:
  - Total emissions (tCO2e): 2019 (baseline) 25,013; 2022 10,642; 2023 11,124; 2024 10,364 — indicating substantial progress toward the −60% target by 2030.
  - Scope 1: 2019 1,020; 2022 622; 2023 692; 2024 853 (2024 increase due to improved data on refrigerants and company-owned vehicles).
  - Scope 2 (market-based): 2019 6,067; 2022 5,065; 2023 3,678; 2024 3,417.
  - Scope 3 business travel: 2019 16,359; 2022 3,224; 2023 4,400; 2024 3,968.
  - Other included scope 3: 2019 1,567; 2022 1,731; 2023 2,354; 2024 2,126.
- Emissions reduction levers and progress:
  - Energy efficiency: Ongoing improvements to premises; property management focuses on energy- and space-efficiency and encourages landlords to upgrade. The 2017–2025 target to cut energy use per m² by 15% has been achieved; a new target will be adopted in 2025. Increasing the share of renewable energy remains a focus.
  - Business travel: Reductions pursued via more virtual meetings, less travel, and more sustainable transport modes. Use of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is possible and can significantly reduce emissions, but SAF-related reductions are not yet reflected in reporting due to evolving calculation and validation methods.
- Stakeholder engagement: Continuous dialogue with stakeholders informs target development, but stakeholders are not directly involved in setting the targets.

nodes.title: Target for own operations
nodes.heading: Target for own operations
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank has a target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from its own opera -tions by 60 per cent by 2030 compared with the baseline year 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Swedbank’s overarching climate target for own operations: cut absolute greenhouse gas emissions 60% by 2030 versus the 2019 baseline (no carbon credits; target stated in absolute tCO2e).
- Coverage and gases: includes scope 1, scope 2 (market-based), and selected scope 3 categories—business travel; security transport services; upstream emissions from energy use and company-owned vehicles; waste; water; and paper. Gases covered: CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, and CFCs (refrigerants).
- Organizational boundary: applies to all home markets and other countries where Swedbank operates, including Norway, Finland, China, and the USA.
- Baseline rationale and governance: 2019 chosen to avoid Covid-19 effects; target set by internal experts, not third-party validated; stakeholders consulted generally but not involved in setting targets; the target’s contribution by scope cannot be specified because it was set jointly across selected GHG Protocol categories based on 2019 data availability.
- Methodology notes: reporting against the target is based on emissions reported in section E1-6; since 2019, measurement scope expanded as data improved (e.g., IT equipment added from 2022) but added sources like IT equipment are outside the target boundary; 2022–2023 historical data have been revised to reflect the target scope for clearer progress tracking.
- Performance highlights and trends:
  - Energy efficiency: 2017–2025 goal to cut energy use per m² by 15% has been achieved; a new target will be adopted in 2025; continued push to raise the share of renewable energy in premises.
  - Scope 1: reported emissions increased in 2024 due to better data availability, notably for refrigerants and company-owned vehicles.
  - Scope 2: continued focus on energy-efficient, space-efficient premises and engaging property owners to improve efficiency.
  - Scope 3 business travel: active reduction efforts via virtual meetings, reducing trips, shifting to more sustainable transport; option to use Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) exists, but current reporting does not account for SAF-related reductions pending robust calculation/validation methods.
- Data presentation: the target is consistent with GHG inventory boundary rules; business travel includes flights, buses, cars, trains, and hotel nights (company-owned vehicle emissions are scope 1, not counted under business travel).

structure.title: Calculation methods
structure.heading: Calculation methods
structure.start_phrase: Calculation methods for calculating Swedbank’s total emissions in scopes 1–3 are presented below.
structure.summary:
- Focus: How Swedbank calculates greenhouse gas emissions across scopes 1–3, aligned with the GHG Protocol, using the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline) with access and quality control by U&We.
- Gases and units: Quantifies all seven Kyoto gases and reports in CO2e using appropriate GWPs.
- Governance and purpose: Methods support tracking of climate targets (referenced in section E1-4); supplier-specific and market instruments are quality-checked by U&We.
- Scope 1 (direct emissions): Covers stationary fuels, heating, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage. Vehicle emissions estimated via financial controls; refrigerants via operational controls using weight/type of gas.
- Scope 2 (purchased energy): Calculated both location-based and market-based for operations under Swedbank’s operational control.
  - Location-based: Uses grid-average factors; robust activity data for electricity, district heating/cooling; for small branches, allocations by employees (FTE) and office area (m2). Emission factors from IPCC, BEIS, AIB, CIBSE, UN. Biogenic CO2 not separated.
  - Market-based: Applies supplier-specific factors tied to contractual instruments (EACs, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights). Instruments covered 37% of 2024 consumption; residual factors used where quality criteria not met or instruments absent. Factors from supplier EPDs/mixes; CH4 and N2O included. Biogenic emissions not separated for district heating; separated for Estonia’s electricity mix.
- Scope 3 (own operations): Includes business travel, security transport, paper, water, waste, and production of employee IT equipment. Calculated with activity data (quantities, pkm, hotel nights, waste weights); no spend-based methods in 2024. Emission factors from IPCC, BEIS, CIBSE, UN, and suppliers. Share of primary supplier data not quantifiable.
- Scope 3 (financed emissions): Internal tool based on PCAF. Financed emissions = Emissions × Attribution factor (bank’s financed share). 2024 saw expanded coverage across the lending portfolio and methodological upgrades.
  - Method improvements: Clarified scopes and data handling for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate; better area data sources and rules for consolidated vs company-level data.
  - Methods by segment: Asset-based for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, Shipping; company-level for Business Loans; top-down country-level for Agriculture and Swedish private Forestry. Sequestration applied for Swedish private Forestry; company-level removals excluded.
  - Comparability: Broader scope and method changes mean figures are not directly comparable with 2023; historical values restated for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and for Steel and Power Generation (target sectors).
- Data and assumptions: Emission factors from recognized databases (IPCC, AIB, BEIS, UN, CIBSE). Where activity data is missing, uses average-vehicle assumptions and allocates small-branch emissions by FTE and floor area per GHG Protocol.
- Boundary and control: Scope 2 and operational data cover branches/buildings under Swedbank’s operational control; Scope 3 also includes investments via Swedbank Robur Fonder.

nodes.title: Scope 1
nodes.heading: Scope 1
nodes.start_phrase: The calculations use emission factors from internationally recognised data- bases such as IPCC, AIB, BEIS and the UN.
nodes.summary:
- Describes Swedbank’s greenhouse gas accounting methodology for scopes 1–3 aligned with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, using the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline); access and quality control (data checks, certificates, calculations) provided by U&We.
- Quantifies all seven Kyoto greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, NF3, SF6, PFCs) in CO2e using appropriate GWPs.
- Scope 1: Direct emissions from stationary fuels, heating, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage; vehicles estimated via Group financial controls; refrigerants via operational controls (refrigerant type and mass).
- Scope 2: Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, district heating/cooling/steam; calculated both location-based (grid-average factors) and market-based (supplier-specific/contractual instruments). Contractual instruments (EACs, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights) covered 37% of 2024 consumption; U&We assessed quality criteria; residual mix used where instruments don’t qualify or aren’t used. Boundary is operations with operational control.
- Scope 2 data and factors: Robust activity data for main operations; electricity purchases reported separately from grid charges; smaller branches allocated by employees (FTE) and floor area (m2). Emission factors from IPCC, BEIS, AIB, CIBSE, UN, and suppliers’ EPDs/specific mixes. CH4 and N2O included. Biogenic emissions generally not separated for location-based and district heating; separated for Estonia’s electricity mix.
- Scope 3 (own operations): Activity-data-based calculations for business travel, security transports, paper, water, waste, and employees’ IT equipment; no spend-based calculations in 2024; emission factors from IPCC, BEIS, CIBSE, UN, and select suppliers; share of primary supplier data not quantifiable.
- Data gaps and allocations: Where activity data is missing (e.g., small branches), emissions allocated using average per FTE and per m2; vehicle fuel assumptions based on an “average vehicle.” Approach follows GHG Protocol and is justified by strong coverage in main operations.
- Financed emissions (lending portfolio): Internal tool based on PCAF Standard. Formula: Financed emissions = underlying emissions × attribution factor (bank’s financed share of company/asset value).
- 2024 portfolio methodology enhancements: Expanded coverage across the full lending portfolio where methods exist; improved methods for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clearer scopes, better data sources, handling area anomalies, clarified consolidated vs company-level rules).
- Asset- and company-level methods: Asset-based for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, Shipping; company-level “Business loans”; top-down country-level for Agriculture and for Swedish private individuals in Forestry.
- Removals and sequestration: No company-level emission removals included; sequestration applied for Swedish private forestry holdings.
- Comparability and restatements: Due to expanded scope and methodological improvements, 2024 results aren’t directly comparable with 2023; historical figures restated for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and for Steel and Power Generation sectors (covered by climate targets).
- Governance and assurance elements: U&We manages platform access, checks market-based certificates against quality criteria, and validates calculations to support tracking against Swedbank’s climate targets (referenced in section E1-4).

nodes.title: Scope 2
nodes.heading: Scope 2
nodes.start_phrase: When calculating location-based scope 2 emissions, Swedbank has robust reporting of activity data in respect of purchased electricity, district heating and district cooling for its main operations.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and framework: Swedbank calculates its greenhouse gas emissions annually using the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline), with access and quality control by U&We. Calculations follow the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, cover all seven Kyoto gases using CO2e and GWP values, and underpin tracking of climate targets.

- Data sources and QA: Emission factors come from recognized databases (IPCC, AIB, BEIS, CIBSE, UN; supplier EPDs for market-based electricity). U&We assesses the quality of market-based contractual instruments. Where activity data is missing, assumptions (e.g., “average vehicle”) and allocation methods are used in line with the GHG Protocol.

- Scope 1 methodology: Direct emissions from stationary fuels, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage. Vehicle emissions estimated via financial controls; refrigerants calculated via operational controls (type and charge). For small branches, emissions allocated using employees (FTE) and office area (m2).

- Scope 2 methodology:
  - Coverage: Purchased electricity, district heating and cooling, and steam for sites under Swedbank’s operational control; electricity purchases (kWh) separated from grid charges.
  - Dual reporting: Location-based uses average grid factors; market-based uses supplier-specific/contract-based factors (EACs, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights).
  - Contractual instruments: Represented 37% of 2024 consumption; where instruments fail quality criteria or are absent, residual mix factors are used. Swedbank does not sell energy (0% sales of certificates).
  - Gases/biogenic treatment: CH4 and N2O included; biogenic CO2 generally not separated (except for Estonia’s electricity mix); district heating biogenic not separated.

- Scope 3 coverage:
  - Own operations: Indirect emissions from business travel, secure transport, paper, water, waste, and manufacturing of employee IT equipment. Calculated from activity data (e.g., weights, passenger-km, hotel nights); no spend-based methods used in 2024. Mix of database and supplier-specific factors; the share based on supplier primary data cannot be quantified.
  - Investments and lending: Scope 3 includes emissions from the lending portfolio and investments via Swedbank Robur Fonder.

- Financed emissions (lending portfolio) methodology:
  - Standard and formula: Internal tool aligned with PCAF; Financed emissions = Emissions × Attribution factor (bank’s financed share of company/asset value).
  - 2024 developments: Expanded coverage to the full portfolio where methods exist; improved methods for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clearer scopes, better data sources, anomaly handling for area data, clarified use of consolidated vs company-level data).
  - Method set: Asset-based methods for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, Shipping; company-level method for Business loans; top-down country-level method for Agriculture and Swedish private Forestry.
  - Removals/sequestration: No company-level removals included; sequestration applied for Swedish private Forestry.
  - Comparability: Due to expanded scope and methodological improvements, 2024 figures are not directly comparable to 2023; historical figures restated for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and target sectors (Steel, Power Generation).

- Allocation approach for smaller units: Where activity data is lacking, emissions for smaller branches are allocated using FTEs and floor area, leveraging Group estimates per employee and per m2, justified by strong data coverage in main operations.

nodes.title: Scope 3
nodes.heading: Scope 3
nodes.start_phrase: Scope 3 was calculated based on activity data such as quantity/weight of pur chased products, passenger kilometres, hotel nights and waste weights.
nodes.summary:
- Swedbank’s greenhouse gas accounting is performed annually on the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline), with access and quality control (input data, market-based certificates, calculations) managed by U&We.
- Methodology follows the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, quantifying all seven Kyoto gases in CO2e using appropriate GWPs.
- Scope 1: Direct emissions from stationary fuels, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage. Vehicle emissions are estimated via Group financial controls; refrigerant emissions are calculated via operational controls using refrigerant type and charge.
- Scope 2: Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, district heating/cooling, and steam. Calculated using both location-based (grid-average factors) and market-based methods (supplier-specific factors and contractual instruments such as EACs, direct contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific mixes). Contractual instruments covered 37% of 2024 consumption; U&We assessed their quality and residual factors were used where criteria were not met or instruments not purchased. Calculations apply to operations under Swedbank’s operational control. Biogenic emissions are generally not separated (exception: electricity mix in Estonia); CH4 and N2O are included. Electricity purchases are tracked separately from grid charges.
- Scope 3 (own operations): Indirect emissions from business travel, security transport, paper, water, waste, and manufacturing of employee IT equipment. Calculated using activity data (e.g., quantity/weight of goods, passenger-km, hotel nights, waste weights). No spend-based calculations in 2024; the share of primary supplier data cannot be quantified.
- Scope 3 (lending portfolio and investments): Financed emissions calculated using PCAF (Financed emissions = Emissions x Attribution factor). 2024 saw expanded portfolio coverage and methodological upgrades, notably for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clearer scopes, improved data sources, anomaly handling for property area data, clarified rules on consolidated vs company-level data). Asset-based methods developed for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, and Shipping; a company-level method (“Business loans”) and a top-down country method for Agriculture and private-individual Forestry in Sweden. Company-level removals are excluded; sequestration is applied for private-individual Forestry. Due to scope expansion and improvements, figures are not fully comparable with 2023; historical data for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and the target sectors Steel and Power Generation have been restated.
- Data, factors, and allocation: Emission factors sourced from IPCC, AIB, BEIS, CIBSE, UN, supplier EPDs, and supplier-specific mixes. Where activity data is missing, assumptions (e.g., “average vehicle”) are applied. For smaller branches, emissions are allocated using FTE and floor area (m2) based on Group averages. This allocation approach is consistent with the GHG Protocol and used sparingly given strong activity-data coverage in main operations.

nodes.title: Scope 3 emissions from own operations
nodes.heading: Scope 3 emissions from own operations
nodes.start_phrase: Scope 3 was calculated based on activity data such as quantity/weight of pur chased products, passenger kilometres, hotel nights and waste weights.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and framework: Describes Swedbank’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emission calculation methods for scopes 1–3, aligned with the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol Corporate Standard and used to track climate targets (section E1-4).
- Tools and governance: Annual calculations performed in the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline); platform access and data/calculation quality control managed by U&We, including review of market-based energy certificates.
- Gases covered: Quantifies all seven Kyoto gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, NF3, SF6, PFCs) in CO2e with applicable GWPs.
- Emission factors and data sources: Uses internationally recognized databases (IPCC, AIB, BEIS, UN, CIBSE, supplier EPDs). Where activity data are missing, applies reasonable assumptions and allocation based on FTE and office area (m2), consistent with the GHG Protocol.
- Scope 1: Direct emissions from stationary fuels, heating, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage. Vehicle emissions estimated via Group financial controls; refrigerants via operational controls (type and weight).
- Scope 2 (location-based): Covers purchased electricity, district heating, and cooling where Swedbank has operational control. Robust activity data for main operations; smaller branches use FTE/area allocations. Emission factors from recognized databases; biomass/biogenic CO2 not reported separately; CH4 and N2O included.
- Scope 2 (market-based): Applies supplier-specific factors reflecting contractual instruments (energy attribute certificates, direct energy contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights). Contractual instruments cover 37% of 2024 consumption. U&We assesses quality; residual mix factors used where criteria are unmet or instruments not purchased. Factors from supplier EPDs or supplier mixes; biogenic emissions not separated for district heating, but separated for Estonia’s electricity mix; CH4 and N2O included. Swedbank does not sell energy.
- Scope 3 (own operations): Based on activity data (e.g., quantities/weights of purchases, passenger-km, hotel nights, waste). No spend-based calculations in 2024. Factors from IPCC, BEIS, CIBSE, UN, and suppliers. Share of primary supplier data cannot be quantified.
- Scope 3 (lending portfolio – financed emissions): Calculated with an internal tool aligned to PCAF. Formula: Financed emissions = Emissions × Attribution factor (bank’s financed share of company/asset value). 2024 saw expanded coverage and improved methods, notably for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (refined scopes, better data sources, handling area-data anomalies, clarified use of consolidated vs company-level data). Asset-based methods developed for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, and Shipping; company-level method for Business loans; top-down country-level method for Agriculture and Swedish private Forestry. Company-level removals excluded; sequestration applied for Swedish private Forestry. Methodological expansions lead to non-comparability with 2023; historical figures restated for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and for Steel and Power Generation sectors under climate targets.

nodes.title: Scope 3 emissions from the lending portfolio
nodes.heading: Scope 3 emissions from the lending portfolio
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank has created an internal calculation tool based on the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) Standard to calculate financed emissions for its lending.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and framework: Swedbank’s greenhouse gas accounting is performed annually on the Our Impacts platform (EcoOnline), with access and quality control by U&We. Calculations follow the WBCSD/WRI GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, cover all seven Kyoto gases, and express results in CO2e using GWP factors. Methods support tracking progress toward climate targets (referenced as E1-4).

- Data quality and sources: Emission factors come from internationally recognized databases (IPCC, AIB, BEIS, CIBSE, UN, plus supplier data). Where activity data is missing, reasonable assumptions (e.g., “average vehicle”) are used. For smaller branches, emissions are allocated by number of employees (FTE) and floor area (m2). The approach aligns with the GHG Protocol.

- Scope 1 (direct emissions): Includes stationary fuels for energy/heating, company-owned vehicles, and refrigerant leakage. Vehicle emissions are estimated using the Group’s financial controls; refrigerants are calculated via operational controls using refrigerant type and weight.

- Scope 2 (purchased energy):
  - Boundary: Operations in branches and buildings under Swedbank’s operational control.
  - Dual reporting: Both location-based and market-based methods are applied.
  - Location-based: Uses grid-average factors; robust activity data for electricity, district heating, and cooling. Electricity purchases are tracked separately from grid charges. For smaller branches, allocations use FTE and m2. Emission factors used do not isolate biomass shares; biogenic CO2 is not separated. Swedbank does not sell energy (0% sales).
  - Market-based: Applies supplier-specific factors and contractual instruments (energy attribute certificates, direct energy contracts, PPAs, supplier-specific rights). Contractual instruments covered 37% of total consumption in 2024. U&We assessed instrument quality; residual mix factors are used where quality criteria are not met or instruments are absent. Emission factors draw on suppliers’ EPDs or supplier-specific mixes. Biogenic emissions are not separated for district heating but are separated for Estonia’s electricity mix. CH4 and N2O are included.

- Scope 3 (value chain emissions):
  - Own operations: Includes business travel, security transport, paper, water, waste, and production of employees’ IT equipment. Calculated from activity data (e.g., passenger-km, hotel nights, waste weights); no spend-based calculations in 2024. Swedbank cannot quantify the share based on primary supplier data.
  - Investments: Includes emissions from the lending portfolio and from Swedbank Robur Fonder.

- Financed emissions (lending portfolio):
  - Methodology: Internal tool based on PCAF Standard. Formula: Financed emissions = Emissions × Attribution factor, where attribution reflects Swedbank’s financed share of the company/asset value. Company-level removals are excluded; sequestration is applied for Swedish private individuals in Forestry.
  - 2024 enhancements: Expanded coverage across the full lending portfolio where methods exist. Improved methodologies for Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate (clearer scopes, better data quality with new sources, handling of property area anomalies, clarified use of consolidated vs company-level data).
  - Method set: Asset-based methods for Real Estate, Motor Vehicles, and Shipping; company-level method for Business loans; top-down country-level method for Agriculture and for Swedish private individuals in Forestry.
  - Restatements and comparability: Due to scope expansion and methodological improvements, 2024 figures are not directly comparable with 2023. Historical values for Mortgages, Commercial Real Estate, and for Steel and Power Generation sectors (with climate targets) have been restated.

nodes.title: Recalculation rules
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.1 Recalculation rules
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank has defined recalculation rules that describes the nature of events that would trigger a recalculation of financed emissions for either the base-year and/or other years, as well as a significance threshold that would be a subject for restatement.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Swedbank’s recalculation rules for financed emissions, detailing when historical data (base year and/or other years) must be restated: structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), methodology changes, improved emission factors/activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), material errors, and addition of new scope 3 categories. Restatements are required when impacts exceed 5% for any target-setting sector/portfolio; smaller changes may be restated to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: mortgages (private persons/tenant-owner associations for housing); commercial real estate (property management companies for revenue-generating properties).
  - Scope: PCAF scope 1 and 2.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × building emissions.
    - Attribution factor: loan-to-value based on baseline market value; for loans originated after 2019, origination value is used.
    - Building emissions: annual kgCO2e from energy use. Sweden uses EPC energy consumption, heated area, heating source, energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates. Baltics use heated area, EPC, and PCAF EPC/building-type estimates; expired EPCs (up to 10 years) may be used. If data are missing, apply estimated heated area and PCAF building-type averages.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: PCAF scope 1 and 2; includes passenger cars, vans, motorcycles, heavy trucks; excludes tractors.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × vehicle emissions.
    - Attribution factor: financing amount divided by market value at origination.
    - Emissions: annual tailpipe or electricity-related emissions; prefer vehicle-specific tailpipe intensity (g/km) × annual distance. If unavailable, use PCAF estimates (make/model/type/fuel). Scope 2 electricity data from PCAF; annual distance inferred from PCAF when missing.

- Shipping:
  - Scope: loans secured by vessels; limited to ships >5,000 GT due to IMO reporting; covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3.
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × vessel emissions.
    - Attribution factor: financing divided by vessel market value at origination.
    - Emissions: annual tCO2e from fuel consumption using fuel- and engine/vessel-type-specific emission factors (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and Forestry:
  - Rationale: business loan approach overestimates for these segments; apply top-down method using National Inventory Reports.
  - Scope: agriculture (dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crops, other agriculture); forestry limited to private persons in Sweden (other forestry uses business loan method).
  - Method:
    - Agriculture: country territorial emissions (scope 1: on-farm and soils; scope 2: energy for machinery) plus limited scope 3 from mineral fertilizer production in core markets.
    - Forestry: includes CO2 sequestration; allocates based on private ownership share.
    - Allocation to Swedbank customers via market share and attribution factor.

- Business Loans (all other corporate lending not covered above):
  - Scope: PCAF scope 1, 2, and 3 (noting incomplete scope 3; PCAF proxies cover upstream only).
  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor × company emissions.
    - Attribution factor: Swedbank loan amount divided by company total assets (company or consolidated level aligned to emissions boundary).
    - Emissions data: customer-reported/public data where available; otherwise PCAF region/industry proxies; in some cases based on physical activity metrics (e.g., MWh). Use latest full-year data not older than 24 months.

nodes.title: Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.2 Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate
nodes.start_phrase: Mortgages are defined as loans to private persons or tenant owner associations for acquiring residential housing.
nodes.summary:
- Recalculation rules: Swedbank defines when financed emissions must be recalculated or restated, including triggers such as group structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, improved emission factors or activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), discovery of material errors, and addition of new Scope 3 categories. Publicly disclosed climate targets and base-year data are updated when impacts exceed a 5% threshold for any targeted sector/portfolio; the bank may also restate for smaller changes to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate: Covers Scope 1 and 2 per PCAF. Financed emissions = attribution factor × building emissions. Attribution factor is the loan-to-value based on baseline market value (and origination value for loans since 2019). Building emissions are annual kgCO2e from energy use. Sweden uses EPC data (heated area, energy consumption, heating source), energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates. Baltics use heated area, EPCs (including estimates and expired EPCs up to 10 years), and PCAF building-type estimates; where data are lacking, estimated heated area and PCAF building-type averages are applied.

- Motor vehicles: Includes passenger cars, light-duty vehicles, motorcycles, heavy trucks; tractors excluded. Covers Scope 1 and 2. Financed emissions = attribution factor × vehicle emissions. Attribution factor is financing divided by vehicle market value at origination. Emissions are annual tailpipe or electricity-related emissions; priority is vehicle-specific tailpipe intensity and annual distance. If unavailable, PCAF estimates by make/model/type/fuel are used; Scope 2 electricity data from PCAF; annual distance implied from PCAF if missing.

- Shipping: Applies to loans secured by vessels; data constrained to ships >5,000 GT (per IMO reporting). Covers Scope 1 and upstream Scope 3. Financed emissions = attribution factor × vessel emissions. Attribution factor is financing divided by vessel market value at origination. Vessel emissions are annual CO2e from fuel consumption using fuel- and engine-specific emission factors (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and forestry: Uses a top-down approach based on National Inventory Reports; business loan method was found to overestimate emissions for these sectors. Agriculture scope includes dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crop growing, and other agriculture; covers Scope 1 and 2 territorial emissions plus Scope 3 limited to mineral fertiliser production in core markets. Forestry applies only to private persons in Sweden; uses CO2 sequestration data and assumed private ownership share; other forestry activities use the business loan method. Allocation to Swedbank is based on market share and attribution factors.

- Business loans: Default method for all other business lending. Covers Scope 1, 2, and 3, noting incomplete Scope 3 coverage and PCAF estimates limited to upstream. Financed emissions = attribution factor × company emissions. Attribution factor is loan amount divided by total assets (company or consolidated, aligned with emissions boundary). Emissions sourced from company disclosures (public or bilateral) or estimated via PCAF region/industry proxies; in some cases based on physical activity (e.g., MWh generated). Financial and GHG data use the latest full-year information, not older than 24 months.

nodes.title: Calculation methodology
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.2.1 Calculation methodology
nodes.start_phrase: Calculations of financed emissions for real estate consist of two parts: the attribution factor and the building’s emissions.
nodes.summary:
- Recalculation and restatement policy: Swedbank defines when financed emissions must be recalculated for the base year and/or other years. Triggers include structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, improved emission factors or activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates, more granular energy-source factors), material errors, and additions of new scope 3 categories. Publicly disclosed base-year data and climate targets are updated when impacts exceed a 5% threshold for any targeted sector/portfolio; optional restatements may occur for smaller changes to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Standards and scopes: Calculations align with PCAF. Each asset class combines an attribution factor with asset/company emissions. Coverage varies by class: real estate and motor vehicles cover scopes 1–2; shipping covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3; agriculture covers scopes 1–2 plus limited scope 3 (fertiliser production); business loans cover scopes 1–3 with noted scope 3 data gaps (PCAF upstream only).

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:
  - Definitions: Mortgages to private persons/tenant-owner associations; CRE to property companies (retail, offices, industrial, multi-family).
  - Method: Attribution via loan-to-value fixed at baseline market value (and origination value for loans opened after 2019). Emissions are annual kgCO2e from building energy use.
  - Data: Sweden uses EPC data (heated area, energy use, heating source), energy-source emission factors, and occupant energy use estimates. Baltics use heated area, EPCs (including estimates and those expired up to 10 years), and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates. If data lacking, use estimated heated area and PCAF building-type factors.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: Passenger cars, light-duty vehicles, motorcycles, heavy trucks; tractors excluded for data limitations.
  - Method: Attribution = financing divided by vehicle market value at origination. Emissions = annual tailpipe or electricity-related emissions. Highest quality uses vehicle-specific tailpipe g/km and annual distance; otherwise PCAF estimates by make/model, vehicle/fuel type. Scope 2 and missing annual distance sourced/estimated from PCAF.

- Shipping:
  - Scope: Loans secured by vessels; constrained by IMO reporting (ships >5,000 GT). Covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3 of vessels.
  - Method: Attribution = financing divided by vessel market value at origination. Emissions from annual fuel consumption and fuel-specific emission factors, reflecting engine type, vessel size/type, and fuel (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).

- Agriculture and Forestry:
  - Scope: Agriculture includes dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crop growing, other agriculture. Forestry applies to activities related to forestry for private persons in Sweden; other forestry activities use the business loan method.
  - Method: Top-down using National Inventory Reports. Agriculture covers scope 1 (operations, cropland/grassland organic soils) and scope 2 (energy), plus scope 3 limited to mineral fertiliser production. Forestry uses national data on CO2 sequestration with an assumption on private ownership share. Allocation to Swedbank based on market share and attribution factors. Results for non-private forestry are included under the business loan method.

- Business Loans:
  - Scope: Default for all business loans not covered by other methods; covers scopes 1–3, with incomplete scope 3 as companies improve methodologies; PCAF estimates only address upstream emissions.
  - Method: Attribution = Swedbank loan amount divided by company total assets (company or consolidated, aligned with emissions boundary). Emissions data sourced from public/bilateral company reports or PCAF region/industry proxies; sometimes activity-based (e.g., MWh generated). Financial and GHG data use latest full-year figures, not older than 24 months.

nodes.title: Motor Vehicles
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.3 Motor Vehicles
nodes.start_phrase: Motor vehicles are defined as financing towards passenger cars, light-duty vehi - cles (vans), motorcycles and heavy trucks.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out Swedbank’s recalculation and restatement rules for financed emissions, including triggers (group structural changes like acquisitions/divestments, methodology changes, improved emission factors or activity data, material errors, and additions of new scope 3 categories) and a 5% significance threshold for sectors/portfolios with climate targets; allows discretionary restatement for smaller changes to ensure consistency and comparability.
- Defines financed-emission calculation frameworks by portfolio, generally using an attribution factor multiplied by asset/company emissions, aligned with the PCAF standard.
- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate: Scope 1 and 2; attribution factor based on loan-to-value at baseline market value (or origination value after 2019); building emissions derived from energy use and emission factors. Sweden uses EPC data, heated area, energy consumption, heating source, and occupant energy; Baltics use EPCs and PCAF EPC/building-type estimates, including expired EPCs (up to 10 years) when necessary; fallback to PCAF building-type estimates and estimated heated area if data are missing.
- Motor Vehicles: Covers passenger cars, vans, motorcycles, heavy trucks (tractors excluded); scope 1 and 2; attribution factor equals financing divided by vehicle’s market value at origination; emissions based on tailpipe intensity and annual distance (or PCAF estimates when missing); electricity-related (scope 2) emissions from PCAF; distance implied from PCAF when unavailable.
- Shipping: Applies to loans secured by vessels; constrained to ships >5,000 GT due to IMO reporting; covers scope 1 and upstream scope 3; attribution factor equals financing over vessel market value at origination; emissions calculated from annual fuel consumption and fuel-specific emission factors reflecting engine, vessel type/size, and fuel (e.g., HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol).
- Agriculture and Forestry: Uses a top-down approach based on National Inventory Reports. Agriculture includes scope 1 (operations incl. cropland/grassland organic soils), scope 2 (energy for machinery), plus scope 3 for mineral fertiliser production; forestry considers CO2 sequestration and private-person ownership share (Sweden only; other forestry activities use the business loan method). Allocation to Swedbank customers is via market share and attribution factors. Notes that the business loan method would overestimate emissions for these sectors based on peer analysis and statistics.
- Business Loans: Default method for all other business lending; covers scope 1, 2, and 3 (scope 3 remains incomplete; PCAF estimates only cover upstream). Attribution factor equals Swedbank loan amount divided by company total assets (company or consolidated level as appropriate). Emissions sourced from customer reports/bilateral data, PCAF region/industry proxies, or physical activity metrics (e.g., MWh). Financial and GHG data are the latest full-year available and not older than 24 months.

nodes.title: Calculation methodology
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.3.1 Calculation methodology
nodes.start_phrase: The financed emissions of motor vehicle loans are calculated by multiplying an attribution factor by the emissions of the vehicle.
nodes.summary:
- Recalculation rules: Swedbank defines when to restate financed emissions for the base year and/or other years. Triggers include structural changes (acquisitions/divestments), significant methodology changes, improved emission factors or activity data (e.g., new PCAF estimates), material errors, and additions of new Scope 3 categories. Public climate targets and base-year data are updated when restatements change any targeted sector/portfolio by more than 5%. The bank may also restate for smaller changes to preserve consistency and comparability.

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate: Defines mortgages (private persons/tenant-owner associations) and commercial real estate (property management for income-generating assets). Uses PCAF, covering Scope 1 and 2. Method = attribution factor (loan-to-value fixed at baseline market value; for loans post-2019, at origination value) × building emissions. Building emissions derive from energy use (kgCO2e/year). Sweden: uses EPC data (heated area, energy consumption, heating source), energy-specific emission factors, and occupant energy estimates for highest quality. Baltics: uses heated area, EPC, and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates; expired EPCs (up to 10 years) may be used; if data lacking, apply building-type and area estimates from PCAF.

- Motor Vehicles: Covers passenger cars, light-duty vehicles, motorcycles, heavy trucks; excludes tractors due to data gaps. Uses PCAF, covering Scope 1 and 2. Method = attribution factor (financing/market value at origination) × vehicle emissions. Emissions per year from tailpipe or electricity use; highest quality uses vehicle-specific tailpipe intensity and annual distance. If unavailable, PCAF estimates by make/model/type/fuel; Scope 2 from PCAF in all cases; distance inferred from PCAF if missing.

- Shipping: Applies to loans secured by vessels; data limited to ships >5,000 GT per IMO reporting rules. Covers Scope 1 and upstream Scope 3. Method = attribution factor (financing/market value at origination) × vessel emissions. Emissions computed from annual fuel consumption volumes and fuel-specific emission factors reflecting engine, vessel size/type, and fuel (HFO, MGO, LNG, biofuel, methanol, etc.).

- Agriculture and Forestry: Uses a top-down approach based on National Inventory Reports by country and sector, as the general business loan method would overestimate emissions for this segment. Agriculture scope includes dairy, livestock, mixed farming, crop growing, and other agriculture. Forestry scope covers activities for private persons in Sweden; other forestry activities use the business loan method. Agriculture includes Scope 1 and 2 territorial emissions (operations; cropland/grassland organic soils; energy for machinery) plus limited Scope 3 for mineral fertilizer production in core markets. Forestry accounts for CO2 sequestration and private ownership share. Allocation to Swedbank is by market share and attribution factors.

- Business Loans: Default method for all other business lending. Covers Scope 1, 2, and 3 of customers; Scope 3 remains incomplete as companies improve coverage; PCAF estimates cover upstream only. Method = attribution factor (Swedbank loan/total assets at company or consolidated level) × company emissions. Emissions sourced from customer public reports, bilateral disclosures, PCAF region/industry proxies, or activity-based estimates (e.g., MWh generated). Financial and GHG data use latest full-year figures not older than 24 months.

- Cross-cutting themes: Heavy reliance on PCAF standards and datasets; clear attribution-factor frameworks; differentiated data-quality tiers and fallback proxies when primary data is missing; sector-specific scope boundaries; and governance for restatements to ensure consistency, relevance, and comparability over time.

nodes.title: Shipping

  - Method: financed emissions = attribution factor x company emissions.

nodes.title: Calculation methodology

nodes.title: Calculation methodology
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.6.1 Calculation methodology

- Mortgages and Commercial Real Estate:

Baltics use heated area, EPC, and EPC/building-type PCAF estimates; expired EPCs up to 10 years may be used; if data is lacking, use estimated heated area and PCAF building-type averages.

- Motor Vehicles:
  - Scope: 1 and 2; tractors excluded due to data gaps.

  - Attribution: company loan amount divided by total assets (company or consolidated, aligned to emission data used).

nodes.title: Deviations from PCAF
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.7 Deviations from PCAF
nodes.start_phrase: The bank has opted for certain deviations from the PCAF standard based on availability or quality of data.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of deviations from PCAF: Swedbank departs from PCAF where data availability/quality is limited, using alternative methods and certain assumption changes.
- Sector-specific methods:
  - Shipping: Uses vessel-level annual data aligned with International Maritime Organization requirements.
  - Agriculture and private forestry in Sweden: Applies top-down estimates using National Inventory Reports, market share, and financing data.
  - Swedish real estate (TOAs and assets with EPCs): Follows Swedish Bankers Association guidance, but uses European Environment Agency electricity emission factors instead of IEA; plans full alignment next year. TOA calculations designed to avoid double counting.
- Assumption deviations:
  - Business loans: Uses company asset value as a proxy for equity and debt in attribution factors due to internal data gaps.
  - Commercial real estate: No updated property valuations upon loan modification owing to system limitations.
  - Motor vehicles: Treats leasing contracts the same as lending per PCAF motor vehicle method.
- Next steps: Ongoing enhancement of financed-emissions methodologies, data quality, and transparency; plans to expand scope 3 category 15 to include facilitated emissions.
- Investments (Swedbank Robur Fonder):
  - Covered under GHG Protocol scope 3 category 15; uses TCFD-aligned WACI; not a PCAF signatory but adopts PCAF equations for financed emissions.
  - Applies to equities and corporate bonds using provider-sourced reported/estimated data.
  - Includes scopes 1 and 2; excludes scope 3 due to low reliability and volatility; cannot quantify the proportion of reported vs estimated data.
  - WACI: Holding carbon intensity × portfolio weight, summed; normalization redistributes weights when data is missing.
  - Financed emissions: Emissions × financed share, where financed share = investment holding / EVIC; summed at portfolio level.
  - Missing data assumptions: Assigns sector or global averages derived from the fund’s portfolio.
- Total GHG emissions and targets (CSRD E1-6):
  - 2024 used as baseline for first CSRD report; other climate targets have 2019/2022 baselines.
  - Lending portfolio targets are sectoral; investment targets are intensity-based; own-operations targets are absolute and not category-specific; no emission-category targets presented; potential future refinement; metrics not externally validated.
- Emissions inventory and materiality:
  - Longstanding own-operations emissions reporting, with ongoing expansion (e.g., review of Purchased goods and services and supplier materiality).
  - Financed emissions calculated for lending and investments to inform transition planning; methodological details provided elsewhere in the report.
  - Materiality assessment finds over 99% of scope 3 emissions stem from customers’ operations and fund investments (category 15); remaining categories (1–14) are immaterial for external reporting but continue to be monitored internally.

nodes.title: Next steps
nodes.heading: 5.2.7.3.2.8 Next steps
nodes.start_phrase: Swedbank continues to develop its calculations and reporting of financed emissions, including by improving data quality and methodological aspects.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of Swedbank’s deviations from the PCAF standard driven by data availability/quality, including custom methods and assumption changes.
