nodes.summary:
- The section presents Swedbank’s EU Taxonomy Green Asset Ratio (GAR) KPI flow for 2024, showing how much of the bank’s covered assets are taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned.
- Two calculation perspectives are disclosed:
  - Turnover-based
  - CapEx-based
- Results are reported across all six environmental objectives:
  - Climate Change Mitigation (CCM)
  - Climate Change Adaptation (CCA)
  - Water and Marine Resources (WTR)
  - Circular Economy (CE)
  - Pollution Prevention and Control (PPC)
  - Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO)
- For each perspective and objective, the tables show:
  - Proportion of total covered assets that are taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned
  - “Of which” breakdowns: use-of-proceeds, transitional, enabling
  - Coverage of total assets
  - Scope: assets included in both numerator and denominator of the GAR (loans and advances, debt securities including use-of-proceeds bonds, equity instruments not held for trading)
- The exposure breakdown covers:
  - Financial undertakings (credit institutions and other financial corporations, including investment firms, management companies, insurance undertakings)
  - Non-financial undertakings
  - Households (including residential mortgages, building renovation loans, motor vehicle loans)
  - Local government financing and collateral obtained
- Key 2024 highlights (Turnover-based):
  - Total taxonomy-eligible share: 35.61% of covered assets
  - Total taxonomy-aligned share: 3.08%, of which 0.02 pp use-of-proceeds and 0.10 pp transitional
  - Households dominate eligibility and alignment: 34.54 pp eligible and 2.73 pp aligned, driven by residential mortgages (34.34 pp eligible; 2.73 pp aligned)
  - Non-financial undertakings: 1.04 pp eligible; 0.35 pp aligned
  - Financial undertakings: 0.03 pp eligible; 0.01 pp aligned
  - Asset coverage: 99.63% of total assets
  - By objective: climate-related categories drive almost all eligibility; CE, PPC, and BIO exposures are minimal (low basis points)
- Key 2024 highlights (CapEx-based):
  - Total taxonomy-eligible share: 35.91% of covered assets
  - Total taxonomy-aligned share: 3.15%, of which 0.03 pp use-of-proceeds, 0.13 pp transitional, and 0.01 pp enabling
  - Households: 34.54 pp eligible; 2.73 pp aligned (largely residential mortgages)
  - Non-financial undertakings: 1.30 pp eligible; 0.42 pp aligned
  - Financial undertakings: 0.07 pp eligible; ~0.00 pp aligned
  - Asset coverage: 99.63% of total assets
  - CE, PPC, and BIO remain negligible under this view as well
- Overall takeaway:
  - Swedbank’s GAR is predominantly driven by residential mortgage exposures.
  - Taxonomy alignment remains in the low single digits, with slightly higher figures under the CapEx-based approach.
  - Non-climate objectives (CE, PPC, BIO) currently contribute marginally to eligibility and alignment.

nodes.title: KPI off-balance sheet exposures
nodes.heading: 5. KPI off-balance sheet exposures
nodes.start_phrase: Turnover based, stock
nodes.summary:
The excerpt presents Swedbank’s 2024 EU Taxonomy key performance indicators for off-balance sheet exposures, focused on how financial guarantees and assets under management (AuM) relate to taxonomy-relevant sectors. It reports both eligibility and alignment as proportions of total eligible off-balance sheet assets, with breakdowns into use-of-proceeds, transitional, and enabling activities, and coverage across the six environmental objectives (climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, water and marine resources, circular economy, pollution prevention and control, biodiversity and ecosystems).

Main elements covered:
- Scope and metrics:
  - Two KPIs: Financial guarantees (FinGuar KPI) and Assets under management (AuM KPI).
  - Four disclosure lenses: turnover-based (stock and flow) and capex-based (stock and flow).
  - For each, disclosure of taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned proportions, and “of which” splits into use-of-proceeds, transitional, and enabling.
  - Objectives covered: CCM, CCA, WTR, CE, PPC, BIO. Tables for CE, PPC, and BIO show no figures, indicating no reported activity in these objectives for the period.

- 2024 total results (summed across objectives):
  - Turnover-based, stock:
    - Financial guarantees: 20.49% eligible; 1.21% aligned; minimal enabling (0.01%).
    - AuM: 14.96% eligible; 1.38% aligned; of which 0.11% use-of-proceeds and 0.56% transitional.
  - Capex-based, stock:
    - Financial guarantees: 22.57% eligible; 3.36% aligned.
    - AuM: 15.51% eligible; 2.23% aligned; of which 0.15% use-of-proceeds and 0.68% transitional.
  - Turnover-based, flow:
    - Financial guarantees: 0.03% eligible; 0.00% aligned.
    - AuM: 8.37% eligible; 1.20% aligned; of which 0.11% use-of-proceeds and 0.52% transitional.
  - Capex-based, flow:
    - Financial guarantees: 0.03% eligible; 0.00% aligned.
    - AuM: 9.63% eligible; 1.75% aligned; of which 0.17% use-of-proceeds and 0.53% transitional.

- Notable takeaways:
  - Capex-based stock shows the highest alignment shares, especially for financial guarantees (3.36%) and AuM (2.23%).
  - Financial guarantees exhibit negligible flow activity and low alignment overall relative to eligibility.
  - AuM shows consistent taxonomy alignment across all views, with meaningful contributions attributed to transitional and use-of-proceeds categories.
  - Reported activity is concentrated in climate-related and water objectives (CCM, CCA, WTR), with no figures shown for CE, PPC, and BIO in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Key ratio per business segment and the groups consolidated KPI 2024
nodes.heading: Key ratio per business segment and the groups consolidated KPI 2024
nodes.start_phrase: Turnover based
nodes.summary:
The excerpt presents Swedbank’s 2024 EU Taxonomy key performance indicators by business segment, shown on both a turnover-based and a capex-based basis, and aggregated to group-level consolidated KPIs. It covers the environmental objectives Climate Change Mitigation (CCM), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Water and Marine Resources (WTR), Circular Economy (CE), Pollution Prevention and Control (PPC), and Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO), with disclosures split into taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned proportions and further broken down into use-of-proceeds, transitional, and enabling activities where applicable.

Key elements:
- Scope and structure:
  - KPIs are reported per segment: Banking (with credit portfolio, financial guarantees), Asset Management, Insurance, Non-financial activities, plus placeholders for Fees and Commissions and Trading Portfolio (to be reported from 2025).
  - Consolidated, weighted-average KPIs are provided for the group.
  - For each objective, the share of total covered assets funding taxonomy-relevant sectors (eligible) and the share that is taxonomy-aligned are shown, including “of which” splits (use of proceeds, transitional, enabling).

- Revenue base and segment weight:
  - Group revenue: SEK 148,290m.
  - Banking dominates revenue (SEK 129,252m; 85.63% of group), followed by Asset Management (SEK 10,988m; 8.29%), Insurance (SEK 5,728m; 4.32%), and Non-financial activities (SEK 2,322m; 1.75%).

- Turnover-based consolidated KPIs (2024):
  - CCM: eligible 48.05%; aligned 2.61% (with very small use-of-proceeds and enabling shares).
  - CCA: eligible 3.03%; aligned 0.01% (enabling near zero).
  - Other objectives: WTR 0.00% eligible/aligned; CE 0.10% eligible, 0.01% aligned; PPC 0.02% eligible, 0.00% aligned; BIO negligible.
  - Total across objectives: eligible 49.23%; aligned 3.05%; with minimal use-of-proceeds and small enabling/transitional components.

- Capex-based consolidated KPIs (2024):
  - CCM: eligible 48.33%; aligned 2.61% (slightly higher enabling and small use-of-proceeds shares than turnover-based).
  - CCA: eligible 3.30%; aligned 0.04%.
  - Other objectives: WTR 0.00% eligible/aligned; CE 0.04% eligible, 0.00% aligned; PPC 0.00% eligible/aligned; BIO negligible.
  - Total across objectives: eligible 49.52%; aligned 3.38%; enabling and transitional categories remain small.

- Segment insights:
  - Banking/credit portfolio account for virtually all taxonomy-eligible and aligned exposure.
  - Financial guarantees, Asset Management, and Insurance contribute marginally.
  - Exposure to WTR, CE, PPC, and BIO is minimal.
  - KPIs for Fees and Commissions and Trading Portfolio will be first published in the 2025 Annual Report.

nodes.title: Taxonomy-aligned economic activities (denominator)
nodes.heading: 2. Taxonomy-aligned economic activities (denominator)
nodes.start_phrase: Turnover based
nodes.summary:
- The section presents 2024 denominators for EU Taxonomy-aligned economic activities across Swedbank’s key green KPIs: Green Asset Ratio (GAR), green ratio for Assets under Management (AUM), financial guarantees, and life insurance, shown both on a turnover-based and capex-based basis.
- It details exposures by specific Taxonomy activities 4.26–4.31, covering nuclear-related activities (pre-commercial technologies, new plant construction/operation, and existing installations) and fossil gaseous fuel activities (electricity generation, high-efficiency cogeneration, and efficient district heating/cooling).
- For each KPI and activity, the tables report gross carrying amounts (SEKm) and the percentage share aligned to climate change objectives, split into total (CCM+CCA), mitigation, and adaptation.
- Headline results indicate low overall alignment shares:
  - GAR: 3.36% aligned on a turnover basis (entirely mitigation, 0% adaptation) and 3.58% on a capex basis (mitigation).
  - AUM: approximately 1.33% aligned turnover-based (about 1.32% mitigation, 0.01% adaptation) and 2.01% capex-based (about 2.00% mitigation, 0.01% adaptation).
  - Financial guarantees: around 1.21% aligned turnover-based and 3.36% capex-based.
  - Life insurance investments: about 1.07% aligned turnover-based (1.06% mitigation, 0.01% adaptation) and 1.37% capex-based (almost entirely mitigation).
- Nuclear categories show small but non-zero aligned exposures; fossil gaseous fuel categories are zero or negligible.
- The vast majority of aligned exposure appears under “Taxonomy-aligned economic activities not referred to in rows 1 to 6,” which drives nearly all reported aligned amounts and percentages.
- A footnote explains the life insurance green ratio as the weighted average of investments directed at, or associated with, Taxonomy-aligned activities.

nodes.title: Taxonomy-aligned economic activities (numerator)
nodes.heading: 3. Taxonomy-aligned economic activities (numerator)
nodes.start_phrase: Turnover based
nodes.summary:
- Context: Extract from Swedbank’s Annual and Sustainability Report 2024, Board of Directors’ report, section “3. Taxonomy-aligned economic activities (numerator).”
- Scope: 2024 EU Taxonomy disclosures presenting the numerator of key green KPIs under two methodologies:
  - Turnover-based and Capex-based.
  - KPIs covered: Green Asset Ratio (GAR), Green ratio for Assets under Management (AUM), Green ratio for financial guarantees, and Green ratio for Life insurance.
  - Figures are shown for combined climate objectives (CCM+CCA) and split between climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation.
- Activities reported: Detailed breakdown for EU Taxonomy activities 4.26–4.31 (nuclear-related and fossil gaseous fuel activities):
  - 4.26 Pre-commercial nuclear technologies.
  - 4.27 Construction/operation of new nuclear power plants (incl. for hydrogen).
  - 4.28 Electricity generation from nuclear energy in existing installations.
  - 4.29–4.31 Electricity/heat from fossil gaseous fuels (incl. high-efficiency co-generation and efficient district heating/cooling).
- Key findings (Turnover-based):
  - GAR: Very small taxonomy-aligned volumes in nuclear (e.g., 27 SEKm, 0.09% in new nuclear; marginal amounts in pre-commercial and existing nuclear). Fossil gaseous fuel activities are essentially zero or rounded to 0.00%.
  - AUM: Small nuclear exposure, notably existing nuclear (e.g., 219 SEKm, ~0.70%); other nuclear categories minimal; fossil gaseous fuels negligible.
  - Financial guarantees and Life insurance: Similarly small exposures to nuclear activities (single- to low-double-digit SEKm, sub‑percentage shares); fossil gaseous fuels negligible.
- Key findings (Capex-based):
  - GAR: Minimal taxonomy-aligned capex in nuclear (e.g., 19 SEKm, ~0.04% for new nuclear); negligible fossil gaseous fuels.
  - AUM: Small capex-linked exposure to existing nuclear (e.g., 122 SEKm, ~0.25%); fossil gaseous fuels negligible to very small (e.g., 5 SEKm, ~0.01% for high‑efficiency co‑generation).
  - Financial guarantees and Life insurance: Trace amounts in nuclear; negligible in fossil gaseous fuels.
- Overall pattern:
  - The vast majority of the applicable KPI denominators are captured under “Taxonomy-aligned economic activities not referred to in rows 1 to 6,” indicating that nuclear/fossil gaseous fuel activities comprise only fractions of a percent of total taxonomy‑aligned exposure.
  - Reported shares are largely associated with climate change mitigation; adaptation components are present but very small.
- Method note: The Life insurance green ratio is defined as the weighted average of investments directed at, or associated with, Taxonomy-aligned economic activities.

nodes.title: Taxonomy-eligible but not taxonomy-aligned economic activities
nodes.heading: 4. Taxonomy-eligible but not taxonomy-aligned economic activities
nodes.start_phrase: Turnover based
nodes.summary:
- Context: Extract from Swedbank’s Annual and Sustainability Report 2024 (Board of Directors’ report) detailing “Taxonomy-eligible but not taxonomy-aligned economic activities” under the EU Taxonomy.
- Scope and period: 2024 disclosures, shown on both a turnover-based and a capex-based basis.
- KPIs covered:
  - Green Asset Ratio (banking book).
  - Green ratio for Assets under Management (AUM).
  - Green ratio for financial guarantees.
  - Green ratio for Life insurance (with a footnote clarifying it is a weighted average of investments directed at Taxonomy‑aligned activities).
  - For each KPI, results are split into Climate Change Mitigation (CCM), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), and combined (CCM + CCA).
- Activities disclosed (EU Taxonomy section 4.26–4.31):
  - Nuclear-related: pre-commercial advanced nuclear technologies (4.26), construction/operation of new nuclear plants (4.27), and electricity generation from existing nuclear installations (4.28).
  - Fossil gas-related: electricity generation from fossil gaseous fuels (4.29), high‑efficiency cogeneration from fossil gaseous fuels (4.30), and production of heat/cool from fossil gaseous fuels in efficient district heating/cooling (4.31).
- Key findings:
  - Exposures to these taxonomy‑eligible but not aligned activities are very small across all KPIs, generally in the range of 0.00%–0.35% of the respective denominators.
  - Among the non‑aligned items, the largest exposures relate to electricity generation from fossil gaseous fuels (with small SEKm amounts appearing across GAR, AUM, and guarantees), while nuclear‑related exposures and district heating are negligible.
  - The denominators of the KPIs are overwhelmingly comprised of “Taxonomy‑aligned economic activities not referred to in rows 1–6,” indicating that almost all reported green ratios are driven by other aligned activities.
- Totals:
  - “Total applicable KPI” lines confirm near‑complete coverage of the denominators and show that the contribution from the non‑aligned eligible activities is immaterial to overall green ratios for GAR, AUM, guarantees, and Life insurance.

nodes.title: Taxonomy non-eligible economic activities
nodes.heading: 5. Taxonomy non-eligible economic activities
nodes.summary:
This excerpt from Swedbank’s Annual and Sustainability Report 2024 (Board of Directors’ report) discloses EU Taxonomy reporting for taxonomy-non-eligible economic activities. It presents 2024 figures in SEK million and their share of the denominator of the applicable KPIs across four KPIs:
- Green Asset Ratio (GAR)
- Green Ratio for Assets under Management (AUM)
- Green Ratio for financial guarantees
- Green Ratio for life insurance

The tables break down non-eligible exposures by specific EU Taxonomy sections related to nuclear and fossil gas activities:
- 4.26 Pre-commercial advanced nuclear
- 4.27 New nuclear power plants
- 4.28 Electricity generation from nuclear in existing installations
- 4.29 Electricity generation from fossil gaseous fuels
- 4.30 High-efficiency co-generation from fossil gaseous fuels
- 4.31 Heat/cool production from fossil gaseous fuels in efficient district systems
and an “Other taxonomy-non-eligible activities” category.

Key points and figures:
- Exposure to the specific nuclear and fossil-gas categories (sections 4.26–4.31) is negligible, with amounts close to zero and reported as 0.00% of denominators (e.g., small amounts in 4.27, 4.28, 4.30; zeros in several cases).
- The bulk of non-eligible exposure sits in “Other taxonomy-non-eligible activities.”

Totals of taxonomy-non-eligible activities in KPI denominators:
- GAR: 844,878 SEKm (44.29%) for Turnover; 839,699 SEKm (44.02%) for Capex.
- AUM: 2,002,487 SEKm (85.04%) for Turnover; 1,989,620 SEKm (84.49%) for Capex.
- Financial guarantees: 6,330 SEKm (79.51%) for Turnover; 6,165 SEKm (77.43%) for Capex.
- Life insurance: 359,212 SEKm (87.80%) for Turnover; 358,033 SEKm (87.51%) for Capex.

Observations:
- Non-eligible shares are modest in the GAR (~44%) but high for AUM (~85%), financial guarantees (~78–80%), and life insurance (~88%).
- The “Other taxonomy-non-eligible” bucket overwhelmingly drives non-eligible exposure across all KPIs.
- A footnote clarifies the life insurance green ratio is a weighted average of investments directed at or associated with Taxonomy-aligned activities.
